workflow_steps.objective: Confirm the approved direction, product and SKU scope, markets, packaging components, production partners, constraints, success criteria, approvals and unresolved inputs.
Validate the selected direction against the fruit-wine category, intended audience, competitive shelf context, price position, sales channels and applicable market requirements.
Translate the validated context into explicit principles for hierarchy, differentiation, shelf impact, legibility, material choices and production consistency.
Define the decision gates, responsibilities, proofing stages, vendor checks, version control and approval path from design refinement through manufacturing handoff.
Resolve the packaging architecture, component formats, dimensions, information hierarchy, content zones and relationships across the intended SKU family.
Create or validate component-specific cutting, folding, bleed, safe-area and glue geometry against manufacturer specifications.
Apply the approved direction to the resolved structures, addressing hierarchy, legibility, materials, finishes, compliance content and production constraints.
Codify the final logo use, typography, colour, imagery, graphic devices and packaging governance needed for consistent production.
Extend the approved system across all confirmed SKUs and components, with controlled differentiation and shared master elements.
Produce and assess representative physical prototypes for scale, assembly, readability, colour behaviour, shelf recognition and SKU distinction.
Build preflighted manufacturing masters with correct separations, colour specifications, bleeds, overprints, linked assets, fonts, finishes and technical annotations.
Validate and package editable masters, press-ready files, dielines, specifications, proofs, usage guidance, version records and approval documentation for final handoff.

missing_inputs: Selected direction files, approval record and list of accepted versus unresolved decisions
Brand assets, identity standards and editable source files
Product positioning, audience, price tier, channel strategy and launch markets
Confirmed SKU list, naming system, product variants and rollout priorities
Final product copy, mandatory statements, claims, ingredients and other jurisdiction-specific regulatory content
Container, closure, label, carton and secondary-packaging requirements
Exact component dimensions, manufacturer-supplied templates and tolerances
Print vendor capabilities, substrate options, colour process, ink limits and finishing constraints
Barcode identifiers, placement requirements and scannability standards
Target unit cost, order quantities, sustainability requirements and procurement constraints
Approved colour references and expectations for proofing or press matching
Required file formats, naming conventions, handoff recipients and ownership of future revisions
Prototype budget, testing criteria, production schedule and approval stakeholders
assumptions: A distinct packaging direction has already been selected by an authorized human stakeholder; this plan does not reopen concept exploration unless validation reveals a material issue.
The final packaging system may need to support multiple fruit-wine SKUs, but the number and differentiation logic remain unconfirmed.
Market research will validate and refine the selected direction without presenting assumptions as evidence.
All dimensions, legal content, colour builds, substrates, finishes and manufacturing tolerances remain provisional until confirmed by the responsible vendors and stakeholders.
Mockups are treated as review aids; production masters, specifications, proofs and approval records constitute the manufacturing handoff.
Applicable regulatory and accessibility requirements will be confirmed for each intended sales jurisdiction by qualified reviewers.
stop_conditions: Do not begin detailed refinement without the selected direction, component scope and authorized approval record.
Pause structural and dieline work until physical formats, dimensions, tolerances and manufacturer requirements are confirmed.
Do not finalize SKU artwork until names, product copy, claims, mandatory content and barcode data are approved.
Do not release production files when preflight identifies missing links, fonts, bleeds, separations, overprint settings or unresolved technical conflicts.
Do not authorize manufacturing until representative prototypes and required proofs have been reviewed against documented acceptance criteria.
Stop final handoff if vendor specifications, stakeholder sign-off, version ownership or the approved production master cannot be unambiguously identified.
rationale: The brief starts from an already selected direction, so the workflow validates its context, establishes production principles and gates, resolves structure and dielines, refines and systematizes the design, expands it across confirmed SKUs, tests physical prototypes, and ends with technically validated production files and a controlled handoff.
